plan.topic: Retatrutide and knee osteoarthritis pain: TRIUMPH-4 Phase 3 (445 adults with overweight or obesity and knee osteoarthritis, 68 weeks, vs placebo), now in fuller publication
plan.angle: Lead with TRIUMPH-4 from Lilly's December 11, 2025 release, called a 'company topline result, not yet peer-reviewed' unless a TRIUMPH-4 journal paper is found and opened. 445 adults with overweight or obesity and knee osteoarthritis, 9 mg or 12 mg vs placebo, 68 weeks. On 12 mg, WOMAC knee pain fell 75.8% on average. In a post-hoc analysis, 12.0% on 12 mg (about 1 in 8) and 14.1% on 9 mg were completely free of knee pain, vs 4.2% on placebo. Don't merge this with the separate TRIUMPH-1 NEJM knee subgroup (80 weeks, up to 61.6% pain reduction). If it's mentioned at all, call it 'a separate, larger trial, now peer-reviewed in NEJM'. Weight-and-knee-load line as a leading explanation: 'likely partly because'. Copy one per-arm discontinuation line exactly from the release. Status: investigational, not approved anywhere as of November 2, 2026; Lilly plans to submit in Q1 2027, and a submission isn't approval. Tirzepatide knee data: separate trials, not head-to-head. No sources, only 'ask a prescriber about approved options or clinical trials'. Exp F line, 'Not personal advice', the prescriber line, then a loop back to the opening question.
plan.working_title: Retatrutide and Knee Pain: What's Confirmed?
plan.why: New retatrutide Phase 3 data is a proven 13:00 peak format (273/206/122 views). TRIUMPH-4 is fresh in publication coverage, and knee pain is a benefit-beyond-weight angle we haven't used. | fact-check: The TRIUMPH-4 core facts check out: 445 adults with overweight or obesity and knee osteoarthritis, retatrutide 9 mg or 12 mg vs placebo, 68 weeks, and up to 28.7% weight loss on 12 mg. WOMAC pain fell 75.8% on 12 mg. Completely free of knee pain at week 68: 14.1% on 9 mg and 12.0% on 12 mg vs 4.2% on placebo. That pain-free figure was described as a post-hoc analysis, so label it. 'About 1 in 8' is accurate for the 12 mg arm only. Don't say 'on retatrutide', because the 9 mg arm was higher. Lilly's planned Q1 2027 US submission is confirmed. Big problem: I could not confirm the claim that TRIUMPH-4 is 'now in fuller publication'. The October 2026 NEJM paper (doi 10.1056/NEJMoa2604169) is TRIUMPH-1, an 80-week trial with a knee OA subgroup of 574. Its WOMAC results are different: up to 61.6% pain reduction and 25% weight loss on 12 mg. Mixing the two trials would be a factual error. Unless a TRIUMPH-4 peer-reviewed paper is found, the TRIUMPH-4 figures come from Lilly's December 11, 2025 topline release and must be called 'not yet peer-reviewed'.

script.hook_pattern: The hook is a familiar "you" moment: knees aching on the stairs. The drug name is on the first frame so muted viewers see it. Then comes an honest "what's confirmed?" answer: company topline results, not yet peer-reviewed, with placebo numbers next to every result and a post-hoc label. The ending loops: the last line, "Back to those stairs", leads straight back into the opening line, "Stairs making your knees ache?"

factcheck.summary: I checked every number in this Short against Lilly's TRIUMPH-4 topline press release (11 Dec 2025), and all of them match. The trial had 445 adults with obesity or overweight, knee osteoarthritis and no diabetes, over 68 weeks against placebo. WOMAC pain fell 75.8% on 9 mg, 74.3% on 12 mg and 40.3% on placebo, using the efficacy estimand, which the script correctly words as "if everyone stayed on treatment". In a post-hoc analysis, 14.1% (9 mg), 12.0% (12 mg) and 4.2% (placebo) had no knee pain; the script labels this post-hoc correctly. Stopping because of side effects was 12.2%, 18.2% and 4.0%. Lilly's Q2 2026 SEC filing confirms the plan to send the BLA to the FDA in Q1 2027. As of today, TRIUMPH-4 has no peer-reviewed paper. TRIUMPH-1, published in NEJM, and TRIUMPH-2, in The Lancet, are separate trials, so "not yet peer-reviewed" is still accurate for this one. Retatrutide isn't approved by any regulator, so "Not approved anywhere" holds. The framing is careful: placebo numbers sit next to every result, the "why" is called untested, the dose comparison isn't overstated, the disclaimer and prescriber lines are there, and there's no dosing advice. The ClinicalTrials.gov record wouldn't load in my fetch tool. Search results confirm the record exists and the trial is completed, but I couldn't check the 21 Jan 2026 "last update" date in its title. The 4 issues below are all minor and optional.

issues.claim: Knee pain scores fell seventy-five point eight percent… Placebo: forty point three.
issues.problem: These are average percent changes from the starting score, and the actual point changes aren't given. Lilly reports −4.5 (9 mg), −4.4 (12 mg) and −2.4 (placebo) points from a baseline of about 6. Viewers may read 75.8% as '75.8% of people got better'.
issues.fix: Change the stat_label to: "Average WOMAC knee pain change from baseline, 9 mg, 68 weeks (−4.5 vs −2.4 points on placebo)". The narration can stay as it is.

issues.claim: We answer one tirzepatide question from the research every day.
issues.problem: This Short is about retatrutide, so a viewer may notice the word 'tirzepatide' doesn't fit. The line is the word-for-word Exp F wording, so this isn't a factual error.
issues.fix: Keep the wording exactly as it is for Exp F consistency. Don't change it unless the experiment owner approves a variant.

issues.claim: The catch: stopping due to side effects.
issues.problem: The most distinctive side effect, dysesthesia (unusual skin sensations), isn't mentioned. The press release reports 8.8% on 9 mg, 20.9% on 12 mg and 0.7% on placebo, mostly mild. Leaving it out is allowed; it's simply a useful extra fact.
issues.fix: Optional, if the word count allows. Add to the s6 narration: "Skin tingling, called dysesthesia, was also more common on retatrutide: up to about one in five on twelve milligrams, mostly mild." Add a list item: "Skin tingling (dysesthesia): 8.8% (9 mg), 20.9% (12 mg), 0.7% placebo".

issues.claim: Not approved anywhere… Ask a prescriber about approved options or trials.
issues.problem: Unapproved retatrutide is widely sold online as a 'research chemical'. One plain safety line would stop viewers from reading positive trial results as a reason to buy it.
issues.fix: Optional. Add to the s7 narration after "applying isn't approval": "Anything sold online as retatrutide isn't an approved medicine." Add a matching on-screen list item: "Online 'retatrutide' isn't an approved medicine".

audio.soundNotes: Music sits well already (−13.5 dB under voice, −13 in pauses); trimmed gain slightly to keep it from creeping toward the loud edge. Tamed three over-loud speech-layer transients (swooshes/blip) that read above the −14 dB floor, thinned a couple of redundant blips in the two chip-reveal swarms, and boosted the near-silent pause swell at 21.1s so that transition actually lands. The two essentially-inaudible swells (10.1s, 35.1s/72.1s) are left alone since gain can't recover a signal that quiet and they're already harmless. Added three bespoke stings for the "catch" twist, the "Not approved" beat (kept deliberately restrained/serious, no bright or playful tone) and the closing disclaimer, per the thin-it-out rule for serious moments.
